title: model-catalog: add filters, compatibility flags, and pricing/limits fields to /models API
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Adds richer filtering and capability metadata to the public model catalog endpoints. This PR introduces query filters for capability-based discovery and model attributes, plus explicit compatibility flags and first-class pricing/limits fields on model descriptors. Motivation: customers have asked for a machine-readable way to pick models by capability (e.g., tool-calling, structured output, streaming-stable) and to programmatically surface cost/limit information for routing and billing. The current /models response is sparse and requires ad-hoc parsing of descriptions in downstream services. What this changes: 1) API surface: GET /v1/models now accepts new query params: 'capability' (comma-separated values: chat, completion, embedding, tool_calling, structured_output, streaming), 'openai_compat' (true|false), 'pricing_tier' (free|standard|premium), and 'min_max_tokens' (min,max). Example: GET /v1/models?capability=tool_calling,structured_output&openai_compat=true 2) Response schema additions: each model object gains optional fields: 'capabilities' (string[]), 'compatibility_flags' (string[]; e.g. "openai_chat", "openai_completion", "openai_embeddings"), 'pricing' (object with flat_rate, per_token_input_usd, per_token_output_usd, currency), and 'limits' (object: max_tokens, max_requests_per_minute, concurrent_requests). These are optional to preserve backwards compatibility; existing clients will continue to work if they ignore new fields. 3) OpenAI compatibility adapter: adapter maps compatibility_flags to legacy OpenAI-style fields for the OpenAI compatibility layer. Added translation layer so openai_compat=true returns aliases expected by older clients. 4) Server-side indexing: index added for capability tags to keep catalog query latency within SLOs (see perf notes below). 5) Docs & SDK: OpenAPI spec updated, python/ts SDKs surface the new fields and query helpers. Compatibility/migration notes: fields are additive and optional; no required fields were changed. The only risk is downstream code that relies on the previous string parsing of model descriptions — we've added an integration test and a migration note in docs. Rollout plan: staged rollout with feature flag 'model_catalog_caps_v1'; default enabled for beta accounts and disabled for strict compat customers. Monitoring: new metrics added: model_catalog.filter_latency_ms, model_catalog.cache_hit_rate, and pricing_field_populated_ratio. Related: Linear ENG-1729 (catalog filter work), PM-404 (pricing requirements). Checklist: - [x] API schema and OpenAPI docs updated - [x] Server implementation of filters and response enrichment - [x] OpenAI compatibility adapter translation layer - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] SDK updates (python + ts) - [x] Perf benchmark added to benchmark-lab - [x] Docs + release notes Notes: see inline snippets below for example response and query. Example response snippet (illustrative): {"id":"rw-mini-1","name":"rw-mini","capabilities":["chat","embedding"],"compatibility_flags":["openai_chat","openai_embeddings"],"pricing":{"per_token_input_usd":"0.00001","per_token_output_usd":"0.00002","currency":"USD"},"limits":{"max_tokens":"4096","max_requests_per_minute":"600","concurrent_requests":"10"}}
commits: feat(models): add capability & pricing fields to model descriptor
feat(api): accept capability/openai_compat query params and wire to controller
chore(sdk): expose model.capabilities helpers in python and ts SDKs
test: integration + perf tests for catalog filters
docs: update /models API docs and migration notes
review_comments: Priya: Please enumerate allowed capability values in the OpenAPI spec and add a small enum for compatibility_flags — this will make SDK generation more reliable.
Maya: Added enum list and OpenAPI examples in models.yaml, and added enum validation in controller.go.
Diego: For pricing fields, prefer per_token_input_usd/per_token_output_usd over input/output_rate to avoid unit confusion. Also add currency field.
Maya: Switched naming per Diego's suggestion and added currency. Also added a note to release_notes about units.
Ethan: One of the integration tests failed on first run due to a race in cache warmup; can we add a short backoff / retry in test harness?
Maya: Fixed test to wait on cache warmup signal; re-ran CI, all green.
release_notes: Added capability-based filtering and machine-readable model metadata: capabilities, compatibility_flags, pricing (per-token input/output), and runtime limits. These fields are optional and additive; SDKs updated to expose helpers. Operators can enable experimental rollout via feature flag 'model_catalog_caps_v1'.
files_to_review_snippets: server/catalog/controller.go: parse capability/openai_compat query params, call store.FilterByCapabilities, enrich results with pricing/limits from model registry
server/catalog/translator_openai.go: map compatibility_flags -> openai.compatibility and provide legacy aliases for openai_compat=true
notes_on_performance: Added an index on model_capabilities (store_sql.go + index_migration.sql) and a small in-memory prefix cache for frequent queries. Benchmark: 99th percentile query latency for capability queries across a 10k model catalog dropped from 180ms to 42ms locally. Metrics added to monitor cache hit rates and filter latency.
migration_instructions: Operators: ensure DB migration index_migration.sql is applied during maintenance window. If you rely on text parsing of model descriptions, switch to the structured 'capabilities' field when ready. Feature flag: model_catalog_caps_v1 toggles population of pricing/limits for existing models; new models will include fields by default.
user_visible_changes: Developers can now call GET /v1/models?capability=tool_calling to discover models that advertise tool calling. Responses will include pricing and limit hints to enable cost-aware routing.
